speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start by saying, Houston, we have a problem.
zh: 我想先说一句：休斯顿，我们有麻烦了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 1969, we landed on the moon for the first time.
zh: 1969 年，我们第一次登上了月球。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same year, we flew Concorde, the faster than the speed of sound airliner.
zh: 同一年，我们让协和式飞机(Concorde)——超音速客机——上了天。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future was supposed to be faster and better.
zh: 未来本该是更快、更好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were supposed to look forward to innovation in air and in space.
zh: 我们本该期待航空和航天领域的创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet half a century later, we can't go to the moon and we can't fly fast in the speed of sound.
zh: 然而半个世纪过去了，我们既上不了月球，也无法以超音速飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only have we lost the ability to go fast, we've lost the ability to do things even at any kind of reasonable speed.
zh: 而且我们不仅失去了快速前进的能力，甚至失去了以任何合理速度做成事情的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was the Wall Street Journal just a couple of weeks ago.
zh: 这是《华尔街日报》几周前的一篇报道。

speaker: Unknown
en: It now takes Lockheed more than two years to build a new Patriot missile interceptor.
zh: 如今洛克希德公司建造一个新的爱国者导弹拦截器需要两年多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is crazy.
zh: 这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is no way to build the future, and this is no way to win a war.
zh: 这不是构建未来的方式，也不是赢得战争的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we look back at history, this is the Boeing 707.
zh: 回顾历史，这是波音 707。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the airliner that brought us into the jet age.
zh: 就是这款客机把我们带入了喷气式飞机时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we fast forward half a century, this is the 787, their latest airliner, which by the way, was launched more than 20 years ago.
zh: 但如果把时间快进半个世纪，这是 787,他们最新的客机——顺便说一句，它早在 20 多年前就已推出。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't spot the difference.
zh: 你看不出区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't fly any faster.
zh: 它并没有飞得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't make the world any more accessible.
zh: 它也没有让世界变得更触手可及。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prior to boom, the closest America ever got to a supersonic airliner was a mock-up.
zh: 在 Boom 出现之前，美国离超音速客机最近的一次是一个全尺寸模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I guess it's all okay because flying's really great, right?
zh: 不过我想这也没关系，因为飞行本来就很棒，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But for me personally, there is nothing so moving as flying.
zh: 但对我个人而言，没有什么比飞行更令人感动的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about that experience of going down the runway, of gathering speed, rushing to hundreds of miles per hour, then climbing into the sky, having this thing that we call a bird's eye view, but it really is a human's eye view.
zh: 想想那样的体验：沿着跑道滑行、加速、冲到每小时几百英里，然后爬升进入天空，拥有我们所说的“鸟瞰视野”——但它其实是“人类视野”。

speaker: Unknown
en: In near-perfect safety, being able to look down at the beauty of the natural world as well as the beauty of everything that humanity has created, we get to ride aboard the wings of Newton and the Wright brothers while taking in the creations of Edison and Rockefeller.
zh: 在近乎完美的安全之中，俯瞰自然世界之美以及人类所创造的一切之美，我们乘着牛顿和莱特兄弟的翅膀，同时领略爱迪生和洛克菲勒的创作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet flying, which should be one of the most inspiring experiences we can ever do, we've turned into something that most people dread.
zh: 然而飞行，这本应是我们所能经历的最激动人心的体验之一，却被我们变成了大多数人畏惧的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we look back in history, it wasn't always this way.
zh: 但回顾历史，事情并非一直如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those first jetliners truly did double the speed of what had come before them.
zh: 那些最早的喷气式客机确实让速度比之前翻了一倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was a double the speed of air travel.
zh: 它让航空旅行速度翻了一倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most important changes were on the ground.
zh: 最重要的变化发生在地面上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hawaii was simply not a tourist destination before the speed of the jet.
zh: 在喷气式飞机的速度出现之前，夏威夷根本算不上旅游胜地。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the ability to get from the US to Honolulu in seven, eight, nine hours that turned Hawaii into a mainstream tourist destination.
zh: 正是能在七、八、九个小时内从美国飞到檀香山的能力，才让夏威夷成为主流旅游目的地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shoes.
zh: 鞋子。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a connection even between air travel and the shoes we wear.
zh: 甚至航空旅行和我们穿的鞋子之间也有联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Phil Knight, the founder of Nike, started the company in the 1960s on a chance trip to Japan when he fell in love with Japanese-style running shoes.
zh: 耐克的创始人菲尔·奈特(Phil Knight),在 20 世纪 60 年代一次偶然的日本之行中爱上了日式跑鞋，由此创办了这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Nike got their start importing Japanese running shoes to America.
zh: 耐克的起步就是把日式跑鞋进口到美国。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or music.
zh: 还有音乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Long before Spotify or Napster, music started to become global.
zh: 早在 Spotify 或 Napster 之前很久，音乐就开始变得全球化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Beatles took the first world tour in the late 1960s, a tour that simply would not have been practical 10 years earlier with slower airplanes.
zh: 披头士在 20 世纪 60 年代末进行了第一次世界巡演——而十年前，用更慢的飞机，这样的巡演根本不可能实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd like to invite you to imagine with me, what would happen if we had another doubling of speed?
zh: 所以我想邀请大家和我一起想象：如果我们再迎来一次速度翻倍，会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would happen if we could cross the Atlantic in three and a half hours?
zh: 如果我们能在三个半小时内横跨大西洋，会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would happen if Sydney were as easy to get to as Honolulu is today?
zh: 如果去悉尼像今天去檀香山一样容易，会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would be the Beatles, the Nikes, and the Hawaii's of a supersonic age?
zh: 超音速时代的“披头士”、“耐克”和“夏威夷”会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: In my mid-20s, I started to think about what it would take to bring back supersonic passenger travel.
zh: 在我二十五六岁的时候，我开始思考要恢复超音速客运旅行需要做些什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I set a lifetime role of breaking the sound barrier.
zh: 我给自己定下了一生的目标：突破音障。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like any tech nerd in my 20s, what did I do?
zh: 于是，像我二十多岁时任何一个技术宅一样，我做了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I put a Google News Alert on supersonic.
zh: 我给“超音速”设了一个 Google 新闻快讯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet there was more progress in supersonic music than supersonic flying.
zh: 然而超音速音乐的进展都比超音速飞行多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I started to wonder, how would it be that supersonic travel could come back?
zh: 于是我开始琢磨：超音速旅行怎样才能回归呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: The obvious thing seemed to be that it would be a private jet, a business jet made by somebody like Gulfstream for the wealthiest people on the planet.
zh: 看似显而易见的答案是：会是一架私人喷气机、一架公务机，由像 Gulfstream 这样的公司为地球上最富有的人制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of the fallouts of the Concorde era was that we actually banned supersonic flight in the US.
zh: 但协和时代的一个后果是，我们实际上在美国禁了超音速飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And since most Gulfstream miles are over land in the US, there simply wasn't much of a business case without a regulatory change.
zh: 而由于 Gulfstream 的大部分里程都是在美国陆地上的，没有监管方面的改变，根本谈不上什么商业前景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nobody in the business jet world wanted to try to change the regulations.
zh: 而公务机圈子里也没人想尝试去改变监管规定。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't want to build an airplane that might not be legal.
zh: 他们不想造一架可能不合法的飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about an airliner?
zh: 那客运班机呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Wouldn't you expect Boeing to carry us forward into a supersonic age?
zh: 你难道不会期望波音带领我们进入超音速时代吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, no, they're not even building new airplanes anymore, let alone innovative new airplanes.
zh: 嗯,不,他们现在甚至连新飞机都不造了,更不用说有创新性的新飞机了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So could a startup do this?
zh: 那么一家初创公司能做到这件事吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all that long ago, the idea of a startup supersonic airliner seemed laughable.
zh: 就在不久之前,一家初创公司造超音速客机的想法还显得很可笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my very many failed investor pitches was in 2015 when Jeff Bezos passed on our seed round at Boom.
zh: 我众多失败的投资者路演之一是在 2015 年,当时 Jeff Bezos 拒绝了 Boom 的种子轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he wrote the 2015 Amazon shareholder letter about how there's certain things that only big companies can do.
zh: 后来他写了 2015 年的 Amazon 股东信,谈到有些事情只有大公司才能做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he cited airliners as one of these.
zh: 他举的例子之一就是客运班机。

speaker: Unknown
en: So an even more laughable idea was what if I could do this?
zh: 所以一个更加可笑的想法是:如果我能做成这件事呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I was a software engineer by training.
zh: 我本来是受过训练的软件工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spent time at early Amazon.
zh: 我们早期在 Amazon 待过一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I founded an apps company that got acquired by Groupon.
zh: 我创办过一家应用公司,后来被 Groupon 收购。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could I do this?
zh: 我能做到这件事吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: My knowledge about airplanes was limited to a pilot's license.
zh: 我关于飞机的知识仅限于一张飞行员执照。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could fly a Cessna.
zh: 我会开 Cessna。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of the things I learned from that time was I didn't think I could really know what I was capable of except by picking a mission that inspired me, something that I wanted to create in the world, and giving it everything I could.
zh: 但我从那段经历中学到的事情之一是,我觉得除非选择一个能激励我的使命,一个我想在世界上创造的东西,并为之倾尽全力,否则我无法真正知道自己有多大能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Only that way could I find my limits.
zh: 只有那样我才能找到自己的极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in 2014, we got started, and it wasn't a very auspicious start.
zh: 所以在 2014 年,我们起步了,而开局并不怎么吉利。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a supersonic airliner mockup made of cardboard, plywood, and seats from Office Depot.
zh: 这是一个由硬纸板、胶合板和 Office Depot 买来的座椅做成的超音速客机模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was before YC.
zh: 那是在 YC 之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the end of YC batch, this is what Boom looked like.
zh: 到 YC 批次结束时,Boom 是这个样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we had a cardboard mockup of our first airliner prototype and people laughed.
zh: 那时我们有了一个第一代客机原型的纸板模型,人们笑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who would name an airplane startup after the sound of an explosion?
zh: 谁会给一家飞机制造公司取一个爆炸声的名字?

speaker: Unknown
en: But we didn't let this deter us and we kept going.
zh: 但我们没有因此却步,我们继续前行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started building our first prototype airliner, XB-1, which started life as baby boom.
zh: 我们开始建造我们的第一架原型机 XB-1,它最初的名字是 baby boom。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't know what it would really take to build a supersonic passenger plane.
zh: 我们不知道建造一架超音速客机到底需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we figured the only way to learn the lessons was to go build, to go build the first supersonic jet made outside of a government or military.
zh: 于是我们认为,学到这些经验的唯一办法就是去建造,去建造第一架在政府或军队之外制造的超音速喷气机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was how XB-1 got started.
zh: XB-1 就是这样开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last year, XB-1 became the first independently developed jet to break the sound barrier, more than a decade after founding the company.
zh: 去年,XB-1 成为第一架突破音障的独立研发喷气机,那是在公司成立十多年之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd like to invite you to relive that moment with me from just about a year ago in the Mojave Desert.
zh: 我想邀请大家和我一起重温大约一年前在 Mojave 沙漠的那个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Historically, the human race has always wanted to go faster.
zh: 纵观历史,人类一直想要更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Control your Gopher Xcel to Mach 1.1.
zh: 控制 Gopher Xcel 加速到 1.1 马赫。

speaker: Unknown
en: Copy Gopher Xcel, cast roll gate.
zh: 收到 Gopher Xcel,cast roll gate。

speaker: Unknown
en: There we are.
zh: 我们到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The XB1 is supersonic, faster than the speed of sound.
zh: XB1 达到超音速了,比音速还快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congratulations, Trepeto.
zh: 恭喜你,Trepeto。

speaker: Unknown
en: You made history today.
zh: 你今天创造了历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congratulations to the whole team.
zh: 恭喜整个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super thankful for you guys.
zh: 非常感谢你们大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future of supersonic travel is looking incredibly promising.
zh: 超音速旅行的未来看起来前景非常光明。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just about speed.
zh: 这不仅仅是关于速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about making the world more connected.
zh: 这是关于让世界更加紧密相连。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've come to believe as a startup founder, you really have to optimize for two days, the worst day and the best day.
zh: 作为一名初创公司创始人,我逐渐相信,你真的必须为两天做优化:最糟糕的一天和最好的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no such thing as a startup that doesn't have tough days.
zh: 不存在没有艰难日子的初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along the way to that flight, Boom nearly failed several times.
zh: 在通向那次飞行的路上,Boom 好几次差点失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a moment where we got down to seven days of cash and the board told me to shut the company down.
zh: 有一个时刻,我们的现金只够撑七天,董事会让我关掉公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I told them, no, we're getting through this.
zh: 我对他们说:不,我们会挺过去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just haven't found the way through yet.
zh: 我们只是还没有找到突破口而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did.
zh: 而我们做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because I believed that what we were creating was important, because I wanted it to exist in the world, I was able to keep going even when it seemed almost impossible.
zh: 正因为我相信我们正在创造的东西是重要的，因为我希望它存在于这个世界上，所以即便在看似几乎不可能的时候，我也能坚持下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because of that, we had to have the best day.
zh: 正因为如此，我们必须拥有最美好的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: That moment where I got to watch the team pull the airplane out of the hangar, watch the pilot push the throttles forward and see that we'd broken the sound barrier.
zh: 那一刻，我看着团队把飞机拖出机库，看着飞行员把油门推向前，看到我们突破了音障。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is why you have to build things that matter, things that matter not just to yourself but to the world, things that inspire you, things that keep you going through the inevitable ups and downs.
zh: 这就是为什么你必须去构建重要的东西，那些不仅对你自己重要、更对世界重要的东西，那些能激励你、让你在不可避免的起伏中坚持下去的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, XB1.
zh: 那么，XB1。

speaker: Unknown
en: accomplished some radical things.
zh: 完成了一些非同寻常的成就。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only did we break the sound barrier, but we did something that we didn't even think was part of the original plan, which is related to solving sonic boom.
zh: 我们不仅突破了音障，还做到了一件我们甚至认为不在原计划之内的事，与解决音爆问题相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: XB1 broke the sound barrier on two flights, six times through the sound barrier, each time no audible sonic boom in the ground.
zh: XB1 在两次飞行中突破了音障，六次穿越音障，每一次地面上都没有可听见的音爆。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually demonstrated a principle that had been talked about for a long time called mock cutoff, where if you break the sound barrier at a sufficiently high altitude and at the right speed for the current weather, the sonic boom actually makes a U-turn in the sky and never touches the ground.
zh: 我们实际上验证了一个被人们谈论了很久的原理，叫做 mock cutoff——如果你在足够高的海拔、并以适合当前天气的速度突破音障，音爆实际上会在天空中掉头，永远不会触及地面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like if a tree falls in a forest and no one's there to hear it, did it really make a sound?
zh: 这就像一棵树在森林里倒下而没人在场听，它真的发出声音了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So by making the sonic boom disappear entirely, we were able to put aside a question that had long plagued people talking about supersonic flight, which is how quiet is quiet enough?
zh: 通过让音爆完全消失，我们得以搁置一个长期以来困扰超音速飞行讨论的问题，那就是多安静才算足够安静？

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's no boom at all, there's nothing to argue about.
zh: 如果根本没有音爆，那就没有什么可争论的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was about 24 hours from breaking the sound barrier to be invited to the West Wing.
zh: 从突破音障到被邀请到白宫西翼，大约只用了 24 小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And 115 days from breaking the sound barrier to an executive order making supersonic flight legal again in the US.
zh: 从突破音障到签署行政令使超音速飞行在美国重新合法化，用了 115 天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, people talk about, isn't it a bad idea to build in a regulated industry?
zh: 是的，人们会说，在一个受监管的行业里创业难道不是个坏主意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out you can change the regulations.
zh: 事实证明，你是可以改变监管规定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way you do it is just by building the thing and communicating why it's okay.
zh: 而改变的方法就是把这个东西造出来，并向人们说明为什么它是没问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: By demonstrating that we could have supersonic flight without a sonic boom, everybody got excited about it.
zh: 通过证明我们可以在没有音爆的情况下实现超音速飞行，所有人都为此感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I like to say that supersonic flight isn't red or blue.
zh: 我喜欢说，超音速飞行不分红党还是蓝党。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's red, white, and blue.
zh: 它是红、白、蓝三色的。

speaker: Unknown
en: After the executive order, a bill dropped in the House and the Senate to make the supersonic legalization permanent.
zh: 在行政令之后，众议院和参议院提出了一项法案，使超音速飞行的合法化成为永久性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It passed the House unanimously.
zh: 它在众议院全票通过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just last week, it got out of the Senate Commerce Committee again with a unanimous vote.
zh: 就在上周，它再次以全票通过了参议院商务委员会。

speaker: Unknown
en: The supersonic flight is coming back.
zh: 超音速飞行就要回归了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were able to do many things for the first time on that airplane.
zh: 我们在那架飞机上第一次实现了很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, the first privately developed supersonic jet.
zh: 首先，是第一架由私营力量研发的超音速喷气机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Previously, this had been the work of governments and militaries with enormous budgets.
zh: 在此之前，这一直是拥有巨额预算的政府和军方的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was also the first supersonic jet made in America.
zh: 它也是第一架在美国制造的超音速喷气机。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first human piloted airplane landed solely on augmented reality with no natural view of the runway.
zh: 是第一架仅依靠增强现实着陆、对跑道没有任何自然视野的有人驾驶飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first supersonic air-to-air live stream filmed on an iPhone streamed via Starlink.
zh: 还有第一部用 iPhone 拍摄、通过 Starlink 直播的超音速空中对空直播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, most importantly, legalizing supersonic flight in the US.
zh: 当然，最重要的是，让超音速飞行在美国合法化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did all of this with a remarkably small team.
zh: 我们是用一支非常小的团队完成这一切的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The XB1 team was just 50 incredibly committed, passionate men and women who were willing to keep going when other reasonable people would have given up.
zh: XB1 团队只有 50 名极其敬业、充满热情的男性和女性，当其他理性的人早已放弃时，他们仍愿意继续前行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how is it that something that used to take billions of dollars and thousands of people was suddenly done by a small team with a comparatively small budget?
zh: 那么，为什么过去需要数十亿美元和成千上万人的事情，突然之间就能由一个小团队用相对较小的预算完成了呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: The key thing is to make hardware development look more like software development, to reduce the cost of iteration, both in the world of bits and in the world of atoms.
zh: 关键在于让硬件开发看起来更像软件开发，无论在比特的世界还是原子的世界里，都要降低迭代的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that look like?
zh: 那是什么样子的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you come in at this from a software perspective, I think we all know that great software is modular.
zh: 如果你是从软件的角度来看这件事的，我想我们都知道，优秀的软件是模块化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you change something in this pit of code over here, it shouldn't change something in the behavior of this code over here, not if it's well designed.
zh: 如果你改动了这边这块代码里的某个东西，不应该改变那边那块代码的行为，前提是设计得当。

speaker: Unknown
en: But great airplanes are incredibly integrated, and everything affects everything else.
zh: 但优秀的飞机是高度集成化的，一切都会影响其他一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best airplane design is interplay of propulsion, of aerodynamics, of structures, of all kinds of optimizations, how you fit the systems into it.
zh: 最好的飞机设计是推进、空气动力学、结构，以及各种优化之间的相互作用，比如如何把系统装配进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we do something like at another row of passenger seats, it makes the fuselage heavier, the engines have to get more powerful, the wings have to get redesigned, everything changes.
zh: 如果我们做出比如再加一排乘客座椅这样的事，机身就会变重，发动机必须变得更强大，机翼必须重新设计，一切都会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so classically, this pace of iteration for complex integrated hardware has been very slow.
zh: 因此，传统上，这种复杂的集成硬件的迭代速度一直非常缓慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine a whole bunch of engineering specialists, each working in an Excel spreadsheet on their own discipline, and then handing off the results of analysis from one engineer to another.
zh: 想象一大群工程专家，每个人在自己的专业领域里用 Excel 电子表格工作，然后把分析结果从一个工程师手里交接给另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So iteration would take very large teams, enormous amounts of time, and eventually you'd have to just say, good enough, it's time to move on and actually build.
zh: 所以迭代需要非常庞大的团队、海量的时间，最终你只能说，够好了，是时候继续前进、真正去建造了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But instead, we took a different approach.
zh: 但相反，我们采取了不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said all of this engineering that historically exists in spreadsheets really should exist in software.
zh: 我们说，历史上存在于电子表格里的所有这些工程工作，其实应该存在于软件中。

speaker: Unknown
en: The spreadsheet engineering is like baby software.
zh: 电子表格工程就像婴儿版的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really code, but it's getting treated like a second-class citizen with no automated integration, no automated testing, no continuous integration, none of that stuff.
zh: 这确实是代码，但它却被当作二等公民对待，没有自动化集成，没有自动化测试，没有持续集成，什么都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we said, let's fix it.
zh: 于是我们说，让我们来解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we built a system called MakeBoom.
zh: 我们构建了一个叫 MakeBoom 的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And MakeBoom lets you literally define an airplane in a configuration file.
zh: MakeBoom 让你能在配置文件里直接定义一架飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can run a script that does a whole aircraft simulation.
zh: 然后你就可以运行一个脚本，做完整的飞机仿真。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in just a few minutes, you can have a good idea of how well your design performed.
zh: 只需要几分钟，你就能对你的设计表现如何有一个大致的了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: How far could it fly?
zh: 它能飞多远?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would its fuel burn be?
zh: 它的油耗会是多少?

speaker: Unknown
en: How many passengers could it carry?
zh: 它能搭载多少乘客?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would the trade-offs be?
zh: 各种权衡会是怎样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And this would allow us not just to evaluate design ideas, it would allow us to go do studies of what airplane we should build.
zh: 这不仅让我们能够评估设计想法，还能让我们去研究我们应该造什么样的飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out of the infinitely many conceivable supersonic jets, what is the correct one to build?
zh: 在无限多种可以设想的超音速喷气机中，哪一种才是正确的选择?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we get to product-market fit?
zh: 我们如何达到产品市场契合?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't get to product-market fit on a supersonic jet by building it and seeing if anybody likes it.
zh: 造一架超音速喷气机，你不可能靠造出来然后看有没有人喜欢来达到产品市场契合。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to analyze very carefully the art of the possible and also what will maximize the market opportunity.
zh: 你必须非常仔细地分析可能性的边界，以及什么能最大化市场机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by being able to understand the universe of conceivably buildable airplanes digitally, we're able to narrow in on the one that we would actually want to go build.
zh: 通过在数字层面理解所有可以建造的飞机的集合，我们能够收窄范围，锁定我们真正想要建造的那一架。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also taking the same approach to how we design our engines, which we're now building for the first time.
zh: 我们对我们设计发动机的方式也采用同样的方法，而这是我们第一次建造发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we built a tool called Blade Runner.
zh: 我们做了一个叫 Blade Runner 的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Blade Runner allows us with really just a couple engineers to change a blade design in real time and see exactly how it's going to behave structurally and aerodynamically.
zh: Blade Runner 让我们只需要几个工程师就能实时修改叶片设计，并确切看到它在结构上和空气动力学上将如何表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: This reduces literally to real time, a process that previously would have taken dozens of engineers many months.
zh: 这把以前需要几十名工程师花费数月的过程，真正地缩短到了实时。

speaker: Unknown
en: So investing in iteration in the world of bits is very important.
zh: 所以在比特世界里投资迭代是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with thanks to AI, the cost of software development is dropping.
zh: 得益于 AI,软件开发的成本正在下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's now possible to have many more software tools than previously would have been possible to build.
zh: 现在可以拥有比以前可能构建的多得多的软件工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you also have to iterate in the world of atoms.
zh: 但你也必须在原子世界里迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the most important things we discovered along the way is it's extremely difficult to iterate with outside suppliers, particularly outside suppliers in aerospace, which are...
zh: 我们在此过程中发现的最重要的事情之一是，与外部供应商进行迭代极其困难，尤其是航空航天领域的外部供应商，它们…

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just say I have no kind words for them.
zh: 可以这么说，我对他们没有任何好话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we chose to build our own machine shop and now we can go from a digitally designed engine part to a prototype part in about 24 hours.
zh: 所以我们选择建立自己的机加工车间，现在我们可以在大约 24 小时内从数字设计的发动机部件做出原型部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is our R&D shop in Denver.
zh: 这是我们在丹佛的研发车间。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a room that does not exist at GE or Rolls-Royce or Boeing or any other large aerospace company.
zh: 这个房间在 GE、罗尔斯-罗伊斯、波音或任何其他大型航空航天公司都不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our engineers are able to work hand in hand with our manufacturing technicians and we're able to go from design idea to part in hours and then iterate much faster than is otherwise possible.
zh: 这样我们的工程师就能与制造技术人员携手工作，我们可以在几个小时内从设计想法到部件，然后以其他方式不可能达到的速度进行迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also vertically integrating our own test assets.
zh: 我们也在垂直整合我们自己的测试资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're building our own engine stand about half an hour from where the engineers and the manufacturing facility exists.
zh: 我们正在距离工程师和制造设施约半小时路程的地方建造我们自己的发动机试车台。

speaker: Unknown
en: This means that when we've got something ready to test, we can test whenever we want.
zh: 这意味着当我们有东西准备好测试时，我们可以随时想测就测。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have to reserve time in someone else's test cell and wait for that slot.
zh: 我们不需要在别人的测试间里预约时间并等待那个时段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens next?
zh: 那么接下来会发生什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: As we're scaling up from XB-1, the test airplane, to Overture, the passenger airliner that we all get to fly on, we have to go big.
zh: 当我们从 XB-1,这架测试飞机，扩展到 Overture,这架我们所有人都能乘坐的客机时，我们必须做大。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're taking our vertically integrated manufacturing and building a super factory that will allow us to build engines and ultimately airplanes at scale.
zh: 我们正在利用垂直整合的制造能力，建造一座超级工厂，使我们能够规模化地建造发动机并最终建造飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what it'll look like when it's complete in just a few months.
zh: 这就是它在仅仅几个月后完工时的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is what it's been like over the last few months.
zh: 而这是过去几个月里的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: In January this was an empty building with a lease that we had just signed and now six months later the first machines are going in and in just a couple weeks we're making our first production engine parts.
zh: 今年一月，这还是一栋空楼，租约我们刚刚签下，而现在六个月后，第一批机器正在进场，再过几周我们就要生产第一批量产发动机部件了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along the way, we solve what was the other hard problem with building a supersonic airliner, which is how do you finance the development?
zh: 在这个过程中，我们解决了建造超音速客机的另一个难题，那就是你如何为研发融资?

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're building something that you know is going to take billions of dollars in R&D capital, and when it's impossible to predict exactly how much capital it will take or exactly how long it will take.
zh: 当你在建造一个你知道将需要数十亿美元研发资本的东西，而且无法精确预测需要多少资本、也无法精确预测需要多长时间的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very, very difficult to raise financing.
zh: 要筹集融资是非常、非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we discovered along the way that because we had made a choice to vertically integrate our own propulsion, we were able to take the engine that we were building for supersonic flight and sell it separately on the ground as a natural gas power turbine.
zh: 但我们在此过程中发现，由于我们做出了垂直整合自己推进系统的选择，我们能够把为超音速飞行而建造的发动机，作为一台天然气动力涡轮机单独在地面销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we call super power.
zh: 这就是我们所说的 super power。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a supersonic engine adapted for ground power generation that can ship without the rest of the airplane, thereby generating the test data, the learnings, the reliability, and also the capital that we need to go big.
zh: 这是一台为地面发电而改造的超音速发动机，可以在没有飞机其余部分的情况下交付，从而产生我们所需要的测试数据、经验教训、可靠性，以及做大所需的资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first super power turbines under construction right now and goes to the first customer in less than 12 months.
zh: 第一批 super power 涡轮机目前正在建造中，不到 12 个月内将交付给第一位客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's take a step back and think about why we're doing this.
zh: 那么让我们退后一步，想一想我们为什么要做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's important to create things that we want to exist in the world.
zh: 我认为创造我们希望存在于世界上的事物是很重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's important to create things that inspire other creators.
zh: 我认为创造能激励其他创造者的事物也是很重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because of that, we chose to live stream XB1's supersonic flight.
zh: 正因如此，我们选择直播 XB1 的超音速飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was the first supersonic installation of Starlink, the first supersonic air-to-air live stream.
zh: 这是 Starlink 首次在超音速环境下使用，也是首次超音速空对空直播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we turned that stream on, millions of people around the world tuned in.
zh: 当我们开启那个直播时，全世界有数百万人观看了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of my favorite shots were from classrooms around the country where kids who were otherwise not tuned into aviation or to science tuned in.
zh: 我最喜欢的画面之一来自全国各地的教室，那些原本对航空或科学不感兴趣的孩子也看进去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of them stood up and some of them jumped up and down.
zh: 有些孩子站了起来，有些孩子跳来跳去。

speaker: Unknown
en: In one of those classrooms somewhere in the world is the next chief engineer of another supersonic jet.
zh: 在世界上某个这样的教室里，坐着另一架超音速飞机的下一位总工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just haven't gotten to meet him or her yet.
zh: 我只是还没能见到他或她。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's important to do that inspiration.
zh: 我们认为做这种激励很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we build in public.
zh: 所以我们公开构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best way to follow along is to follow me or follow the company on X.
zh: 你可能以为大数定律适用于初创公司，但它其实不适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we have actually quite a bit of time for Q&A.
zh: 现在我们其实有不少时间可以做问答。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd love to make this interactive.
zh: 所以我很想让这场活动变成互动式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to make this a conversation.
zh: 我很想让这变成一场对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can send your question to the Y Combinator agent, they are filtering them backstage and we'll pop them up here and we'll talk about them.
zh: 如果你能把问题发给 Y Combinator 智能体，他们在后台筛选问题，会把问题弹到这里，我们来讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is something widely believed in tech that's just not true?
zh: 科技界有哪些广泛被人相信但其实不真实的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Boy, lots of things.
zh: 哎呀，很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was one false belief that almost stopped me from founding Boom.
zh: 但有一个错误信念差点让我没能创立 Boom。

speaker: Unknown
en: You tend to get told that every technology gets created kind of at the earliest moment of history that it could be.
zh: 人们往往会告诉你，每一项技术都是在历史上最早可能的时刻被创造出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore, if your idea is any good and nobody else is working on it, there's probably something wrong with the idea.
zh: 因此，如果你的想法很好却没有其他人在做，那这个想法可能有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there's something wrong with you.
zh: 也可能是你有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then investors ask you the question, why now?
zh: 然后投资人会问你这个问题：为什么是现在？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all of this kind of compounds to a whole bunch of founders running at a relatively small space of ideas that are only recently possible.
zh: 这一切叠加起来，导致一大堆创始人只在最近才变得可能的、相对狭小的一块想法空间里奔跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is why we've got an explosion of AI companies now and why a little while ago we had an explosion of like photo sharing apps.
zh: 这就是为什么现在 AI 公司爆炸式增长，而前段时间我们经历的是照片分享应用的爆炸式增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's not true.
zh: 但这不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many, many unsolved problems in the world, many great ideas hiding in plain sight that were actually solvable, that could have been multi-billion or multi-trillion dollar businesses a while ago, but nobody's building them.
zh: 世界上有非常非常多未解决的问题，许多藏在显而易见之处的伟大想法其实是可解的，它们本来在若干年前就可以成为数十亿甚至数万亿美元的生意，但没有人去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not for any reason other than nobody went and did it.
zh: 而原因不是别的，只是没有人去做而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: The technology for supersonic flight existed actually a long time before Boom was founded.
zh: 超音速飞行的技术其实在 Boom 创立之前很久就已经存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technologically, the company could have been created 10 years earlier.
zh: 从技术上讲，这家公司本可以早 10 年创立。

speaker: Unknown
en: But nobody started it.
zh: 但没有人去创立它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The law of large numbers you might think applies to startups just doesn't.
zh: 你可能认为大数定律适用于初创公司,但其实并不适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world is a smaller place than we're told.
zh: 世界比我们被告知的要小。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I deeply believe that you should pick a problem that you want to go solve in the world and don't worry too much about the answer to why now.
zh: 所以我深信，你应该选择一个你真正想解决的世界问题，不要太纠结「为什么是现在」的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to why now can be because I started now.
zh: 「为什么是现在」的答案可以是：因为我是现在开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it possible for America to actually compete with China on manufacturing at scale?
zh: 美国真的有可能在中国擅长的规模化制造上与之竞争吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have to do it smartly.
zh: 但我们必须聪明地去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: It won't work to try to repatriate
zh: 试图把

speaker: Unknown
en: The manufacturing that left the US.
zh: 离开美国的制造业迁回来是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't beat China at its own game.
zh: 你不会在 China 自己的玩法上击败它。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you do is invent the future, invent the next wave of manufacturing and build that here.
zh: 你要做的是发明未来，发明下一波制造浪潮，并在这里把它建造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can give you some examples of that.
zh: 我可以举一些例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the ways that China hollowed out American manufacturing was by kind of hoovering up the tool and dye industry.
zh: China 掏空美国制造的方式之一，就是大量吞并工具模具行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And which used to be big in the US.
zh: 而这个行业过去在美国规模很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if any of you are not hardware people, one of the things you need to understand about building hardware is you have to make custom precision molds, tools, and fixtures to create your precise parts.
zh: 如果你们中有人不是做硬件的，你需要理解建造硬件的一件事是：你必须制造定制的精密模具、工装和夹具来制作你的精密零件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, so for example, for a...
zh: 你知道，比如说，对于一个……

speaker: Unknown
en: A carbon fiber wing.
zh: 一个碳纤维机翼。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a mold the size of the wing, the contour of the wing, in which you lay up layers and layers of carbon fiber fabric and then cure in that mold to make your wing.
zh: 有一个和机翼一样大小、符合机翼轮廓的模具，你在里面一层一层地铺碳纤维布，然后在那个模具里固化来做出你的机翼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or for metallic parts, you might have stainless steel tools in which you injection mold or make wax masters that then go through some other complex process.
zh: 或者对于金属零件，你可能有不锈钢工装，你在里面注塑成型或制作蜡模母版，然后经过其他一些复杂工艺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the downside of all this tooling, a couple fold.
zh: 而所有这些工装的坏处，有好几个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is because so much manufacturing went to China, the tool and dye industry in the US basically died.
zh: 一个原因是大量制造业转移到了中国,美国的模具行业基本消亡了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very, very hard to find tool and dye engineers in the US.
zh: 而且在美国要找到模具工程师非常非常困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you throw a baseball in China, you'll hit one.
zh: 但在中国扔一颗棒球,就能砸中一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of what we're doing at Boom is trying to figure out how to get rid of the tooling entirely.
zh: 所以我们在 Boom 做的很多事情,就是试图弄清楚如何完全摆脱模具。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, for our turbine blades, we're working in an all-digital manufacturing process that will let us go in 24 hours from a digital design to the most advanced turbine blade in the world with absolutely no tooling.
zh: 举例来说,对于我们的涡轮叶片,我们正在采用全数字化的制造流程,让我们能在 24 小时内从数字设计做出世界上最先进的涡轮叶片,完全不需要任何模具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that example matters because this is, I think, how we win versus China.
zh: 这个例子很重要,因为我认为这就是我们战胜中国的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't win in a game where the most labor is what matters.
zh: 我们不会在一场以劳动力多寡为决定因素的游戏中获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't win at a game where having the tool and die industry is what really matters.
zh: 我们也不会在一场以拥有模具行业为关键因素的游戏中获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to invent the next generation of manufacturing and scale that here.
zh: 我们需要发明下一代制造方式,并在这里把它规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because what America is still best at is invention and freedom and innovation.
zh: 因为美国最擅长的仍然是发明、自由和创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: In what ways has AI made building in the physical world easier?
zh: AI 在哪些方面让在物理世界中构建变得更容易了?

speaker: Unknown
en: What things remain really hard?
zh: 哪些事情仍然非常困难?

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing I think we've seen is that the AI has dramatically reduced the cost of software development.
zh: 我认为我们看到的第一件事是,AI 大幅降低了软件开发的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what that means is that we can have custom engineering tools that otherwise would have been unaffordable to create.
zh: 这意味着我们可以拥有定制化的工程工具,否则创建这些工具的成本是负担不起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was lucky to start my career at Amazon in 2001 when my family thought it was a bookstore.
zh: 我很幸运在 2001 年开始在 Amazon 职业生涯,当时我家人还以为它是一家书店。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that was, I think, great about Amazon culture is they built their own business software to run their own business.
zh: 我认为 Amazon 文化中很棒的一点是,他们为自己的业务构建自己的业务软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the personalization algorithms that power the recommendations on the websites, the things that power people who bought this item also bought.
zh: 比如为网站推荐提供支持的个性化算法,也就是支持「买了这个商品的人也买了」的那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of that was in-house software.
zh: 所有这些都是内部软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The backend software was also completely custom.
zh: 后端软件也完全是定制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The things that would power the warehouses and the delivery trucks, et cetera.
zh: 支持仓库和送货卡车等等的那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is a part of why Amazon was able to be the winner in e-commerce is that they had software that fit the business operation like a glove.
zh: 我认为这是 Amazon 能够成为电子商务赢家的原因之一,就是他们拥有像手套一样贴合业务运营的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to do that in the early 2000s required scale.
zh: 但在 2000 年代初做到这一点需要规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: That much software couldn't have been created by a small company with a small operation.
zh: 那么多软件不可能由一家小公司、小规模的运营创造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what AI does is reduce the cost of building custom software, which I think allows more businesses to have software that fits them perfectly.
zh: 而 AI 做的是降低构建定制软件的成本,我认为这让更多的企业能够拥有完全贴合自己的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that's traditionally inefficient about custom software, or really software at all, is that people building the software, the people using the software are in two different companies and two different organizations, and they don't necessarily understand each other very well.
zh: 定制软件——或者说所有软件——传统上低效的一点在于,构建软件的人和使用软件的人分属两家不同的公司、两个不同的组织,他们不一定很了解彼此。

speaker: Unknown
en: But AI allows anybody who is a user to become a tool builder.
zh: 但 AI 让任何使用者都能成为工具构建者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's a really, really big deal.
zh: 我认为这是一件非常非常大的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's what AI has already made better about building the physical world.
zh: 所以我认为这就是 AI 已经让在物理世界构建变得更好的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's left is we don't really have great physical world AI yet.
zh: 我认为剩下的部分是,我们还没有真正出色的物理世界 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like programming a CNC machine is still an incredibly manual task.
zh: 比如给 CNC 机器编程仍然是一项极其手动的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And despite lots of pitches about AI for industrial automation, we haven't yet seen much that works, but I think that's going to come.
zh: 尽管有大量关于工业自动化 AI 的推介,我们还没有见到多少真正能用的东西,但我认为这会到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, what do I look for when hiring people?
zh: 好,我招人时看重什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one of, for me, this has been one of the most difficult things to really learn and to get right, is building the team.
zh: 这是对我来说最难真正学会并做对的事情之一,就是组建团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in particular at Boom, the last company entrepreneur founded that went on to build a commercial airliner was Douglas Aircraft in 1921.
zh: 特别是在 Boom,上一个由创业者创立并最终造出商用客机的公司是 1921 年的 Douglas Aircraft。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is an industry that has not had startups for an incredibly long time.
zh: 所以这是一个已经极其长时间没有初创公司的行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has only kind of big companies, Boeing, Lockheed, et cetera, that are really terrible cultures.
zh: 它只有那种大公司,波音、洛克希德等等,而这些公司的文化非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we often found that we had this tension between being able to hire people who are technically competent, who are good culture fits, and who are really experienced.
zh: 所以我们经常发现,在能够招到技术能力强的人、文化契合的人、以及真正有经验的人之间,存在这种矛盾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I found is...
zh: 所以我发现的是……

speaker: Unknown
en: That when looking for, you know, to truly value early career talent, people who are young, ambitious, smart, who have not yet been destroyed by working at one of the legacy big aerospace companies, value people who are hands-on, who've gone out into the world and built smart, gets things done, optimistic.
zh: 在寻找、真正重视早期职业人才时,那些年轻、有雄心、聪明、还没有被老牌大型航空航天公司的工作所摧毁的人,要重视那些动手能力强的人,那些走出去、构建过东西、聪明、能把事情做成、乐观的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: At senior levels, it gets even harder.
zh: 在高层级别,这就更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's one of the reasons why when you're building a company, if you can manage to promote from within people that you've grown up in your own culture, that is much, much better.
zh: 这也是为什么当你在创建公司时,如果你能设法从内部提拔那些在你自己的文化中成长起来的人,那会好得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some products that Boomerai wished existed?
zh: 有哪些 Boomerai 希望存在的产品?

speaker: Unknown
en: From a boom perspective,
zh: 从 Boom 的角度来看,

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually delivering on physical AI for manufacturing would be huge.
zh: 真正实现制造业的物理 AI 将会是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like imagine a large format manufacturing capability that could go from a CAD design to an automatically QA'd part with one machine without a programmer.
zh: 比如想象一种大尺寸制造能力,能在一台机器上、不需要程序员,从 CAD 设计到自动通过质检的零件。

speaker: Unknown
en: That would be incredible.
zh: 那将不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no reason to believe that's impossible.
zh: 没有理由认为那是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just hasn't been created yet.
zh: 它只是还没有被创造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: For an early hardware startup in a regulatory gray zone, do you engage regulators before deploying or deploy first and legitimatize after?
zh: 对于一家处于监管灰色地带的早期硬件初创公司，你是先与监管机构沟通再部署，还是先部署然后在事后使其合法化？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we make that call with boom?
zh: 我们在 boom 身上如何做这个决定？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think this is one size fits all.
zh: 我不认为这有一套适用于所有情况的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is very contextual what you should do.
zh: 我认为你该做什么是非常看具体情境的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, in building Uber, Travis basically ignored the regulators and built the service anyway, built a fan base of customers that he could use against the regulators that were trying to shut him down.
zh: 举个例子，在打造 Uber 的过程中，Travis 基本上无视了监管机构，照样把服务做了起来，积累了一大批粉丝用户，他可以利用这些用户去对抗那些试图关掉他的监管机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if Uber had tried to befriend the regulators first, it just wouldn't have worked.
zh: 我认为如果 Uber 当初试图先讨好监管机构，那是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of those reasons is that there was an active opponent, right?
zh: 其中一个原因是，当时有一个活跃的对手，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the entrenched taxi industry.
zh: 比如根深蒂固的出租车行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: was using the regulators to block their competition.
zh: 它们利用监管机构来阻挡自己的竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, this is the pattern in a lot of regulation.
zh: 顺便说一句，这是很多监管背后的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't come from like some well-meaning person trying to keep the public safe.
zh: 它往往不是来自某个好心的、想保护公众安全的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It comes from some entrenched, frankly, lazy interest that doesn't want to have to compete and runs to DC or runs to the local regulator and tries to use the power of government to shut their competition down.
zh: 它来自某个根深蒂固的、坦白说很懒惰的利益方，不想参与竞争，于是跑到华盛顿或者跑到地方监管机构那里，试图利用政府的力量把竞争对手关掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is deeply unethical, but it happens all the time.
zh: 我认为这是极不道德的，但这种事一直在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can do what Travis did and go launch your product and have your customers be your ally, I think that can work great.
zh: 所以，如果你能像 Travis 那样，先推出你的产品，让你的客户成为你的盟友，我认为那可以非常有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was never going to work in aviation.
zh: 在航空业，那套做法是永远行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the other hand, we didn't really have an entrenched enemy.
zh: 而另一方面，我们其实并没有一个根深蒂固的敌人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Boeing has plenty of its own self-inflicted problems.
zh: Boeing 有 plenty 自己造成的麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: They thought boom was kind of cute, would probably never succeed.
zh: 他们觉得 boom 挺可爱的，大概永远不可能成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in a certain sense, we were flying under the radar.
zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们是在雷达之下飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that context, and also building a product that was safety critical, it made a lot of sense to engage regulatory early.
zh: 在那种情境下，再加上我们在打造的是一个安全攸关的产品，尽早与监管机构沟通就非常合理了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we started the company, started building XB1, I went to the FAA, I told them what we were doing, why we were doing it, why we thought it mattered, and we asked them to help us.
zh: 所以当我们创办公司、开始建造 XB1 时，我去了 FAA，告诉他们我们在做什么、为什么做、为什么我们认为这很重要，然后我们请他们帮助我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We asked them for feedback.
zh: 我们请他们给反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said, hey, come anytime you want, see anything you want to see.
zh: 我们说，嘿，任何时候想来就来，想看什么就看什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you see us doing something that we could do better, please tell us.
zh: 如果你看到我们有哪里可以做得更好，请告诉我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to show you our plans before they're finalized so you can give us feedback and we want to listen.
zh: 我们会在计划定稿之前给你们看，好让你们给我们反馈，而且我们愿意倾听。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we found was that the approvals process for XB1, that even for an R&D airplane can stretch on for months, actually happened in 90 minutes from when we said we think we're ready to fly and FAA said, here's the paperwork, we agree, go.
zh: 结果我们发现，XB1 的审批流程——即使是对于一架 R&D 飞机，审批也可能拖上好几个月——实际上只用了 90 分钟，从我们说“我们认为自己可以试飞了”，到 FAA 说“这是文件，我们同意，去吧”。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got the first ever permit for flying a civil supersonic airplane, supersonic, even before the airplane had flown for the first time.
zh: 我们拿到了有史以来第一张民用超音速飞机飞行的许可，超音速，甚至是在这架飞机完成首飞之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We engaged early, we made the regulators part of the team, and we worked together.
zh: 我们很早就开始沟通，我们把监管机构变成了团队的一部分，我们一起合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We made it boom plus FAA versus the problem, not boom versus FAA.
zh: 我们把它变成了 boom 加 FAA 对抗问题本身，而不是 boom 对抗 FAA。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the best piece of advice I ever received?
zh: 我收到过的最好的建议是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about...
zh: 我想到……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about what Steve Jobs talked about in his Stanford's Commencements address, which I assume many of you have seen, but if not, you should watch it.
zh: 我想到 Steve Jobs 在他的斯坦福毕业典礼演讲中谈到的东西，我想你们很多人都已经看过了，但如果没看过，你应该去看一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've watched it, go watch it again.
zh: 如果你已经看过，那就再去看一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he talks about what it takes to do great work and how it's important if you're going to do great work to work on something you love and the importance of not compromising on that and holding out to find that thing that you really want to go build, that you really want to go do, because that's the only way to build something great.
zh: 他谈到了要做出伟大的工作需要什么，以及如果你要做伟大的工作，去做你热爱的事情有多么重要，不要在这点上妥协、要坚持等到你真正想去建造的那个东西、你真正想去做的那件事，因为那是成就伟大作品的唯一途径，这一点很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this also harkens back to the earlier question about what I look for in people.
zh: 我认为这也呼应了前面那个关于我在人身上看重什么的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most important things to look for in people are those who actually care.
zh: 在人身上最重要的品质之一，是那些真正在乎的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can teach skills, you can teach knowledge, you can learn any kind of engineering, but the one thing I've never been able to teach somebody else is to care when they just didn't care.
zh: 你可以教技能，你可以教知识，你可以学任何一种工程，但有一样东西我从来没能在别人身上教会的，就是在他们根本不在乎的时候让他们在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is an important thing to look for in your partners personally, professionally, and your employees, people who care.
zh: 这是在你的伙伴、你的职业关系以及你的员工身上值得寻找的重要品质——那些在乎的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ooh, what's the worst piece of advice I've received and why?
zh: 哦，那我收到过的最糟的建议是什么，为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The worst piece of advice, so my mom, hi mom, my mom told me not to start boom.
zh: 最糟的建议……我妈，嗨妈，我妈叫我不要创办 boom。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what she said was, shouldn't you work on something you know something about?
zh: 她说的是，你难道不应该去做一些你了解的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is common well-meaning advice, right?
zh: 这是常见的善意建议，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: When I started my first company, I figured I knew e-commerce from my time at Amazon.
zh: 当我创办我的第一家公司时，我觉得凭我在 Amazon 的经历，我懂电商。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had been at one of the very first mobile app companies, so I thought I knew mobile.
zh: 我曾待过最早一批移动应用公司之一，所以我觉得我懂移动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I thought I should work on mobile e-commerce because my resume said that's where I would have expertise.
zh: 所以我觉得我应该做移动电商，因为我的简历表明那是我有专长的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, so I actually knew how to do mobile e-commerce, but I had no idea what mobile e-commerce should be.
zh: 是的，我确实知道怎么做移动电商，但我完全不知道移动电商应该是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually didn't really give a shit about anything we were building.
zh: 而且说实话，对我们正在做的任何东西我都根本不在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so although I cranked out, you know, high quality apps, I wasn't having a good time and I had no product vision.
zh: 所以虽然我快速做出了，你知道的，高质量的应用，但我过得并不开心，而且我没有任何产品愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the worst advice is like work on what you know.
zh: 所以我认为最糟的建议就是“去做你懂的事情”这类。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you know can be changed, particularly in a world where everyone has personalized AI tutors, anybody with passion and dedication can learn new knowledge and learn new skills.
zh: 你所知道的可以被改变，尤其是在一个人人都有个性化 AI 导师的世界里，任何有热情和投入的人都能学习新知识、学习新技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what you can't change easily is what you love.
zh: 但你无法轻易改变的是你所热爱的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Knowledge is changeable, passion is not, and never has there been more reason to work on what you love.
zh: 知识是可变的，热情不是，而且从来没有比现在更有理由去做你热爱的事情了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took Boom about 10 years just to break the sound barrier.
zh: Boom 花了大约 10 年时间才突破音障。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, oof.
zh: 是啊，唉。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you convince investors to give a deep tech company enough runway to survive that long before there's a real payoff?
zh: 你如何说服投资者给一家深科技公司足够的跑道，让它在真正回报到来之前撑过那么长的时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't recommend following our footsteps in this regard.
zh: 在这方面我不推荐效仿我们的脚步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Boom nearly died many times.
zh: Boom 好几次差点死掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took a lot more time and a lot more money even to get to a real proof of concept than I expected.
zh: 所以有两点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so two things.
zh: 所以有两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, I mean, with the benefit of hindsight, we were very early to deep tech.
zh: 第一，我是说，事后来看，我们做深科技做得太早了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Had we known on day one what I think the whole community knows today, it wouldn't have taken five years.
zh: 如果第一天我们就知道今天整个行业都已经知道的东西，那就不会花五年。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would have taken more like two or three, and it would have been much easier.
zh: 而是更像两三年，而且会容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if I say, okay, what are the specific lessons behind that?
zh: 所以如果我说，好，这背后的具体教训是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of it is about iteration.
zh: 部分在于迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the most important iteration in hardware, by the way, is to iterate at the product level.
zh: 顺便说一下，硬件领域最重要的迭代，是在产品层面进行迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: We bit off an extremely challenging prototype challenge in XB1.
zh: 我们在 XB1 上给自己定了一个极其艰难的原型挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we should have planned is something simpler and easier that would give us multiple shots on goal.
zh: 我们本应该规划的是更简单、更容易的东西，能让我们多次射门得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that is how you discover not only have you gotten engineering decisions wrong, maybe you've gotten requirement decisions wrong.
zh: 因为只有这样你才能发现，不仅是工程决策可能错了，也许需求决策也错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do that, you can iterate faster, you can get to proof points faster, and the fundraising challenge that Boom had is not one you'll have.
zh: 如果你这么做，你就能更快地迭代，更快地拿到证明点，而 Boom 遇到的融资难题就不会出现在你身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess I recommend not following our footsteps in that regard.
zh: 所以我想我建议不要在那方面效仿我们的脚步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would I work on if I was 20?
zh: 如果我是 20 岁，我会做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think founders should work on the most exciting thing that they can imagine themselves doing with a stretch wherever they are in life.
zh: 我认为创始人应该去做他们能想象自己在人生当前阶段、带一点超越性地去做的最令人兴奋的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're 20, if you have a startup that is like calling you,
zh: 所以如果你是 20 岁，如果你有一个像是在呼唤你的创业想法，

speaker: Unknown
en: that you think about day or night.
zh: 让你日思夜想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you're not even sure whether you can pull it off, but if you're in that state, you should go build that thing.
zh: 也许你甚至不确定自己能否做到，但如果你处于那种状态，你就应该去把那个东西做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't have that, you should go work with the best people you can find solving the problem they're working on that you're most excited about solving.
zh: 而如果你没有那样的想法，你就应该去找你能找到的最优秀的人，加入他们正在解决、而你也是最兴奋想去解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The magic happens early in your career when you find an intersection of what you love doing
zh: 魔法发生在你职业生涯的早期，当你找到你所热爱做的事情的交点，

speaker: Unknown
en: That you can become really good at that matters to the organization around you.
zh: 你能在这件事上变得真正出色，并且它对你周围的组织很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you hit all three of those, your career goes vertical.
zh: 当你同时命中这三点，你的职业生涯就会垂直上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: At early Amazon, I was lucky to get to work on something that Jeff Bezos cared about that mattered to Amazon.
zh: 在早期 Amazon，我很幸运能去做一件 Jeff Bezos 在乎、且对 Amazon 重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there I was, I was like 23, 24.
zh: 就这样，我当时大概 23、24 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a $300 million P&L with a project that one of the world's greatest entrepreneurs cared about.
zh: 我手里有一个 3 亿美元的损益表，做一个世界上顶级企业家之一在乎的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I screwed up, I had the most significant people at Amazon telling me how I screwed up and trying to help me not fail.
zh: 所以当我搞砸的时候，Amazon 最有分量的人会告诉我我是怎么搞砸的，并努力帮我不要失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the kinds of things that are game-changing experiences to have early in your career.
zh: 这些就是那种在职业生涯早期就能改变游戏规则的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: So go work with great people on a problem you care about that matters to the organization you're in.
zh: 所以，和优秀的人一起，去解决你在乎的、对你所在的组织重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's a startup that you want to go create, that you love, that you can't get out of your system, then don't wait, just go start it.
zh: 而如果那是你想去创建的创业公司，你热爱它、它在你心里挥之不去，那就别等了，直接去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: On paper, you didn't have the credentials to start Boom, but you did it anyway.
zh: 纸面上看，你并没有创办 Boom 的资历，但你还是做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where did that self-belief come from?
zh: 那种自信从何而来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can it be cultivated?
zh: 它可以培养吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Truth be told, I didn't have the self-belief on day one.
zh: 说实话，第一天我并没有那种自信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had nowhere close to the resume to build a supersonic airliner.
zh: 我的履历离建造一架超音速客机所需要的水准差得很远。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I told my friends I was thinking about it, I could just watch their eyes roll back and the oxygen would have left the room.
zh: 当我告诉朋友们我在考虑这件事时，我能看到他们翻白眼，房间里的氧气仿佛都被抽走了。

speaker: Unknown
en: One friend told me, like, call me back when you got something less pie in the sky.
zh: 一个朋友对我说，等你有点不那么异想天开的东西时再打给我吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I started thinking about the founders that I admired the most, the Steve Jobses, the Bill Gates.
zh: 但我开始思考我最敬佩的那些创始人，那些 Steve Jobs 们、Bill Gates 们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in particular about something that Bill said in the 1970s.
zh: 我尤其会想起 Bill 在 1970 年代说过的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bill said his goal for Microsoft was to put a personal computer in every home and on every desk running Microsoft software.
zh: Bill 说，他对 Microsoft 的目标是让每个家庭、每张桌子上都有一台运行 Microsoft 软件的个人电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was at a time where personal computers mostly didn't exist.
zh: 那是在个人电脑大多还不存在的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only does he want to make them exist, he's going to put them everywhere and he's going to own the market.
zh: 关于如何自学难的东西,我有什么建议吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, Microsoft did that, and then some.
zh: 当然,微软做到了,而且做得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what was it like to be Bill on that day?
zh: 但是在那一天,作为 Bill 是什么样的感受?

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody comes down and taps you on the shoulder and says, by the way, you're the one.
zh: 没有人会走下来拍拍你的肩膀说,顺便说一下,你就是那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out of all the billions of people that could have done this incredible thing, you're the one that's actually to do it, so here's the confidence, go.
zh: 在所有可能做成这件了不起的事的几十亿人当中,你才是真正会去做的那个人,所以这是你的信心,去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: That conversation never happens.
zh: 那样的对话从来不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one gives you that permission.
zh: 没有人会给你那种许可。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a thing I came to believe was that the only way to know what I was capable of was to pick something that I worked really hard at and give it everything I got.
zh: 而我逐渐相信的一件事是,要知道我能力的唯一办法,就是选一件我真正努力去做的事,并倾尽全力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to stop worrying about whether I could do it and to put all my mental energy on how to do it.
zh: 然后停止担心我能不能做到,而把我全部的心智精力放在如何做到上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the self-belief actually came late, you know, and there's still some days I get up and think, oh man, this is hard.
zh: 所以自信其实来得很晚,你知道,到今天还有些日子我起床后会想,天啊,这太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I pull this off?
zh: 我能做到吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that kind of self-doubt is normal.
zh: 我觉得那种自我怀疑是正常的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to put it aside, do it anyway, and become the person you need to become to succeed at what you've set out to do.
zh: 你必须把它放到一边,照样去做,并且成为你想要做成的事情所需要成为的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, what did I learn from working at Amazon in the early days and any lessons from Bezos?
zh: 好,我从早期在亚马逊工作学到了什么?从 Bezos 那里有什么经验教训?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have an enormous, enormous respect for Jeff and I was very lucky to get to work with him even a little bit when I was young.
zh: 我对 Jeff 怀有极大的、极大的敬意,我很幸运在年轻时能哪怕和他有一点共事的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one of the things that Amazon did really well that is difficult to do together is to think very long range while having incredible operating discipline in the moment.
zh: 我认为亚马逊做得非常好的一件事,而且是一件很难同时做到的事,就是在当下拥有极强的运营纪律的同时,进行非常长远的思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Jeff liked to make kind of seven-year business plans.
zh: 所以 Jeff 喜欢做那种七年期的商业计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because of that, he would tackle things that seemed bizarre to much of the rest of the world.
zh: 正因为如此,他会去攻克在世界其他大部分人看来很怪异的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was laughed at internally and laughed at by his board when he launched Amazon Web Services.
zh: 当他推出 Amazon Web Services 时,他在内部被嘲笑,也被他的董事会嘲笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was laughed at by the world for e-commerce.
zh: 他因电子商务被全世界嘲笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet both of those stories ended really well.
zh: 然而这两个故事最终结局都非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can tell a lot of a character of a company, particularly a public company, by its quarterly behavior.
zh: 我认为你可以从一家公司的季度行为看出它很多的品性,尤其是上市公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it got to the end of a quarter, Amazon would never massage their choices to try and make earnings look good that quarter.
zh: 当一个季度接近尾声时,亚马逊绝不会为了那个季度的财报好看而修饰他们的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just take the long term cash flow decisions.
zh: 他们只做长期的现金流决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet at the same time, there was incredible operating discipline.
zh: 然而与此同时,他们又有极强的运营纪律。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were goals, operational excellence, focus on the here and now.
zh: 有目标、卓越运营、聚焦当下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think doing those two things together, a vision that exists long range and the operational excellence day to day, that's unusual.
zh: 我认为同时做到这两件事——一个长远存在的愿景和日复一日的卓越运营——是不寻常的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's rare.
zh: 这很罕见。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is what great companies are made of.
zh: 但伟大的公司正是由这些构成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You taught yourself the fundamentals of aerospace engineering.
zh: 你自学了航空航天工程的基础知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I have any advice about how to teach yourself hard things?
zh: 关于如何自学难的东西，我有什么建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's important to know...
zh: 我认为重要的是要知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: The difference between knowing enough to pass a test and really understanding something.
zh: 「知道到能通过考试的程度」和「真正理解一件事」之间的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at least for me going through school, you know, I got mostly good grades, but I didn't understand half of what I was actually doing.
zh: 至少对我而言,上学的时候,你知道,我的成绩大多不错,但我并不真正理解我实际在做的事情的一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not really deep down, not first principles.
zh: 不是发自内心深处的理解,不是第一性原理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as I was learning aerospace engineering, I bought textbooks.
zh: 但在我学航空航天工程的时候,我买了教科书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went back and I did remedial, Khan Academy, physics and calculus because I hadn't had any since high school.
zh: 我回过头去补课,用 Khan Academy 学物理和微积分,因为高中以后我就再没碰过这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was doing the problem sets.
zh: 我在做习题集。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I started making a list that I called my confusion list, which is my list of things I didn't think I really understood, even if I could answer the question on a test or answer the question plausibly.
zh: 然后我开始列一个清单,我称之为我的困惑清单,就是那些我不觉得自己真正理解的事情的清单,即使我能答对考试题目或者看起来合理地回答问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my goal was every week to take one thing off the confusion list.
zh: 我的目标是每周从困惑清单上拿掉一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out that was wildly optimistic.
zh: 结果证明那实在太乐观了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The confusion list grew without bound because I was always finding things that I wish I understood completely that I just didn't understand yet.
zh: 困惑清单无限制地增长,因为我总是在发现那些我希望自己完全理解、但当时还不理解的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what it created in myself is a mental awareness of that difference between, I really get this?
zh: 但它在我心中培养出一种心智上的觉察,能分辨「我真的懂了这个?」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm kind of waving my hands.
zh: 还是我只是在含糊其辞地比划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that self-awareness, I think, really matters because when there's a thing that you don't know yet that you need to know, you can stay on it and do whatever it takes cognitively until you have that internal sense of clarity, of not being confused.
zh: 所以我认为那种自我觉察非常重要,因为当有一件你还不知道但你又需要知道的事情时,你可以一直盯着它,在认知上不惜一切代价,直到你拥有那种内在的清晰感、不再困惑的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see, there's a lot of uncertainty about what jobs will look like as AI develops.
zh: 让我想想,随着 AI 的发展,工作会变成什么样,这有很多不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have advice to early career technical people about what skills to learn?
zh: 你对早期职业阶段的技术人有什么关于该学什么技能的建议吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all this AI doomerism is like deeply wrong and confused.
zh: 我认为所有这些 AI 末日论都是深刻错误和混乱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my biggest piece of advice is don't worry about it.
zh: 所以我最大的建议是,别担心这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just go do useful things.
zh: 去做有用的事就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as an example, the notion that software engineering is dead, I just don't buy it.
zh: 举个例子，有人说软件工程已经死了，我根本不信。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Boom, we need far more software engineers in a post-AI world than we would need in a pre-AI world.
zh: 在 Boom,在 AI 之后的世界里，我们需要的软件工程师远比 AI 之前的世界要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the cost of software development has dropped.
zh: 因为软件开发的成本下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anybody, including hardware engineers, can now become a coder.
zh: 任何人，包括硬件工程师，现在都可以成为程序员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need software engineers to make sure the architectures are right and make sense and are coherent.
zh: 而我们需要软件工程师来确保架构是正确的、合理的、连贯的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our need for software engineers has actually gone up as the cost of software engineering has gone down.
zh: 所以随着软件工程成本的下降，我们对软件工程师的需求实际上上升了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the thing that, again, I think let's go back and think about what really matters from first principles, what will be true over a long period of time.
zh: 所以，还是那句话，让我们回到第一性原理，思考什么才是真正重要的，什么是长时间内依然成立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being able to discover what's useful in the world and go learn how to do it and go create something that's real, working with other people, being multidisciplinary.
zh: 能够发现世界上什么是有用的，去学习怎么做，去创造真实的东西，与他人合作，做到跨学科。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like one of the reasons I went to Amazon early in my career is I knew that I'd be able to work on software for marketing and I didn't know Jack about marketing and I wanted to learn it.
zh: 比如我职业生涯早期去 Amazon 的原因之一，就是我知道我能在营销软件上工作，而我当时对营销一无所知，我想学它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so finding a way to kind of see things from multiple perspectives matters, but mostly go find something you want to create and go create it.
zh: 所以，找到一种从多个角度看问题的方式很重要，但最重要的还是去找一个你想创造的东西，然后去创造它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't worry too much about being replaced.
zh: 不要太担心被取代。

speaker: Unknown
en: In software, young builders have an edge.
zh: 在软件领域，年轻的建造者有优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: In hardware, experience seems to win.
zh: 在硬件领域，经验似乎能取胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: High barriers, deep expertise required.
zh: 门槛高，需要深厚的专业知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does a young engineer break in and actually stand out?
zh: 年轻工程师如何打入这个行业并真正脱颖而出?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't believe the premise of the question.
zh: 我不相信这个问题的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: In hardware, experience wins.
zh: 在硬件领域，经验取胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one of these lies told by old people at big, dumb companies, and it's just not true.
zh: 这是大蠢公司里的老人讲的一种谎言之一，它根本不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, all those people suck.
zh: 顺便说一句，那些人都很烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So don't worry about it.
zh: 所以别担心这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go build real things.
zh: 去造真实的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go have hobbies.
zh: 去培养爱好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you're into airplanes, do RC model airplanes.
zh: 比如你喜欢飞机，就玩遥控模型飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And learn not just how to design things, but learn how to actually make them.
zh: 不仅要学怎么设计东西，还要学怎么真正把它们做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the barriers are not actually that high.
zh: 而且门槛其实没那么高。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just go do this stuff.
zh: 你就是可以直接去做这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So don't try to become a deep expert.
zh: 所以不要试图成为深度专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: The moment you become an expert, what you're steeped in is the past, and then you're completely useless.
zh: 一旦你成了专家，你浸润的就是过去，然后你就完全没用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't listen to all the people that tell you you need ages and ages of experience.
zh: 也不要听那些告诉你需要长年累月经验的人的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is one thing about experience that matters, though.
zh: 不过，关于经验，有一件事是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have developed a rule about this at Boom.
zh: 我们在 Boom 为此制定了一条规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is totally okay for a young engineer to do something they've never done before, just the way it's okay for them to do something that nobody has ever done before.
zh: 年轻工程师去做一件他们从未做过的事，是完全可以的，就像他们去做一件世界上从来没人做过的事一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if somebody has done it before in the world, our rule is you have to go find one of those people, call them and ask them your advice.
zh: 但如果世界上有人曾经做过这件事，我们的规则是，你必须去找那样的人，打电话给他们，询问他们的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to take it.
zh: 你不必采纳。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just have to hear it.
zh: 你只需要听到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I find it's very rare that there are experienced, accomplished people that aren't willing to take that call and some form of passion and to give you that advice.
zh: 而且我发现，很少有有经验、有成就的人不愿意接那个电话、带着某种热情来给你那些建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So go seek that wisdom where it's out there, but don't listen to it too much and just go build.
zh: 所以，去寻求那些存在的智慧吧，但也别太听它的话，尽管去造就是了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I recommend starting a company or working at a company early in your career?
zh: 你建议在职业生涯早期是创办公司还是去公司工作?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think this is a one-size-fits-all.
zh: 我不认为这有一个放之四海而皆准的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the moment you have a startup that you desperately want to start, a thing that you want to go create, even if you're not sure how to do it, even if you worry you might fail, but you can't get that idea out of your head, I think at that point you should go start it.
zh: 我认为，当你有一个你拼命想创办的初创公司，一个你想去创造的东西，即使你不确定怎么做，即使你担心可能会失败，但你就是无法把这个想法从脑子里赶走，我认为在那一刻你就应该去创办它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't wait.
zh: 而且不要等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the world is full of examples of great companies that were started by young people.
zh: 世界上充满了由年轻人创办的伟大公司的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world is also full of great companies that were started a little bit later in life.
zh: 世界上也充满了在人生稍晚阶段创办的伟大公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started Boom when I was 33.
zh: 我创办 Boom 时是 33 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started my first company in my parents' basement in high school, an internet service provider that I basically started because I wanted to get a better internet connection and I needed a way to finance it and starting an ISP was the way to do it.
zh: 我创办第一家公司是在高中的时候，在我父母的地下室里，那是一家互联网服务提供商，我创办它基本上是因为我想要更好的网络连接，而我又需要一种方式来给它融资，创办一个 ISP 就是实现这一点的办法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right out of college, I didn't really know what startup I wanted to start.
zh: 大学刚毕业时，我其实不知道自己想创办什么样的初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I went to work at Amazon and got some great experience there.
zh: 于是我去 Amazon 工作，在那里获得了很棒的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't think this is any size fits all.
zh: 所以我不认为这有什么放之四海而皆准的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't start a company just to start a company.
zh: 而且,不要为了开公司而开公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good recipe for misery.
zh: 那是通往痛苦的好配方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the worst thing you can do is start a company that you don't love and then get stuck.
zh: 你能做的最糟糕的事,就是开一家你不热爱的公司,然后被困在里面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this sounds like a champagne problem, but it's actually pretty bad.
zh: 这听起来像个“香槟酒问题”(凡尔赛式的烦恼),但它实际上相当糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know successful founders that have had this problem who are running successful companies that they actually don't love, but they feel the debt of responsibility to their employees and their investors.
zh: 我认识一些有过这种问题的成功创始人,他们经营着成功的公司,但实际上并不热爱,却对员工和投资者感到有责任的重担。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very hard to replace a founder CEO.
zh: 而且,更换一位创始人 CEO 是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now they're trapped.
zh: 所以现在他们被困住了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So start a company, but only if it's a company you want to keep.
zh: 所以,去开公司吧,但前提是它必须是一家你想一直经营下去的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It says we've got time for three more questions.
zh: 上面写着,我们还有时间再回答三个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do founders need to move to San Francisco?
zh: 创始人需要搬到旧金山吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: This founder moved from San Francisco to start Boom.
zh: 这位创始人就是从旧金山搬出来创办 Boom 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I left San Francisco and moved to Denver to put Boom there because it did not seem...
zh: 我离开了旧金山,搬到丹佛,把 Boom 设在那里,因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: feasible to build in the physical world affordably at scale in the Bay Area.
zh: 在湾区以可负担的成本在物理世界中进行规模化制造,看起来并不可行。

speaker: Unknown
en: That said, I do think there's enormous benefit in being surrounded by other ambitious people.
zh: 当我大约 15 岁的时候,我在我家乡辛辛那提可能是唯一的一家软件公司得到了第一份真正的软件工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is no ecosystem better than that than what exists here in San Francisco.
zh: 而没有任何一个生态系统比旧金山这里的生态系统更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let me put it this way.
zh: 所以,让我这样说吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless there is a specific reason why the...
zh: 除非有特定的理由说明为什么……

speaker: Unknown
en: You should not be in an ecosystem.
zh: 你不应该待在一个生态系统里。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should be in an ecosystem.
zh: 你应该待在一个生态系统里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think San Francisco, LA, Austin.
zh: 比如旧金山、洛杉矶、奥斯汀。

speaker: Unknown
en: Be around other people that will inspire you.
zh: 身边要有能激励你的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would I look for in a freshman or sophomore in college who doesn't have work experience yet?
zh: 对于还没有工作经验的大一或大二学生,我会看重什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Side projects.
zh: 课余项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was something like 15, I got my first real software job at what was probably the only software company in Cincinnati where I grew up.
zh: 在我大约 15 岁的时候，我在我长大的地方辛辛那提大概是唯一的一家软件公司，得到了我的第一份真正的软件工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think because I did okay in an interview and I built some things on the side and they felt like they just kind of had to give me a chance.
zh: 我想是因为我面试表现得还不错,而且我在课余做了一些东西,他们觉得他们就是得给我一个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Boom, we will hire people early career with no work experience, but they have to have done something else that demonstrates having been extraordinary.
zh: 在 Boom,我们会雇用没有工作经验的早期职业人士,但他们必须做过其他能证明自己非凡的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want, for example, to come work at Boom, go to BoomSupersonnet.com slash careers, and there's a job opening that's called Your Dream Job.
zh: 所以,比如说,如果你想来 Boom 工作,去 BoomSupersonnet.com/careers,那里有一个职位空缺,叫做“你的梦想工作”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's basically go create whatever you want to go do.
zh: 它基本上就是:去做任何你想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in doing that, you have to tell us something extraordinary about yourself, something that makes you really stand out.
zh: 但在做的过程中,你必须告诉我们一些关于你的非凡之处,一些能让你真正脱颖而出的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't have work experience yet, just show the most impressive thing that you've built on the side and show it with pictures.
zh: 如果你还没有工作经验,就展示你在课余做过的最令人印象深刻的东西,并配上图片展示。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how you can bootstrap yourself.
zh: 这就是你自我起步的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I find this is true of a lot of good people.
zh: 而且我发现很多优秀的人都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: They find a way to do things that are normally young ages.
zh: 他们在通常很年轻的时候就找到了做事的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this notion of like, oh, you have to be like a junior in college to get an internship.
zh: 所以那种说法,比如,“哦,你必须到大三才能得到实习机会。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Nope, that's baloney.
zh: 不,那是胡说八道。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the best people have gotten internships way earlier than that, and you can do it too.
zh: 所有最优秀的人都远早于那个时候就得到了实习机会,你也可以做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, does work-life balance matter?
zh: 好的,工作与生活的平衡重要吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think...
zh: 我认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe in work-life harmony.
zh: 我相信工作与生活的和谐。

speaker: Unknown
en: This notion that there's life and work and there's somehow an opposition doesn't make any sense to me.
zh: 这种认为存在生活和工作、并且两者 somehow 处于对立状态的观念,在我看来毫无道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have meaningful work, it is a big part of your life and the meaning of your life.
zh: 如果你有有意义的工作,它是你生活的重要组成部分,也是你人生意义的重要组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I believe we spend so much of our energy doing our work that we should find work that we love, that is meaningful, that is not just punching in and punching out.
zh: 而且我相信,我们花费了如此多的精力在工作上,所以我们应该找到我们热爱的、有意义的工作,而不只是打卡上班、打卡下班。

speaker: Unknown
en: When there was one more thing I wanted to add to my life, but I couldn't find a way to do it.
zh: 当我想在生活中再增加一件事,但我找不到办法去做的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I started Boom, I had three kids under the age of two.
zh: 当我创办 Boom 时,我有三个不到两岁的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't easy, but I made it work.
zh: 那并不容易,但我让它成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can have a family and be a good dad and be a good CEO too.
zh: 你可以拥有一个家庭,既做一个好爸爸,也做一个好 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not easy, but it can be figured out.
zh: 这不容易,但它是可以被想出办法解决的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, I find that being a parent and being a good CEO is very synergistic.
zh: 事实上,我发现做父母和做一个好 CEO 是非常相辅相成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I take a parenting lesson and bring it to work and find it's the exact same leadership lesson at the office that was part of how helped me with the kids.
zh: 有时我会把一个育儿经验带到工作中,发现它和办公室里的领导力经验一模一样,而它曾是我带孩子的方法之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it cross-pollinates all the time.
zh: 所以它们一直在相互授粉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do things in your life that you love.
zh: 去做你生活中你热爱的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't let detritus into your life.
zh: 不要让废物进入你的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't let things that are not meaningful soak up your time and energy and passion.
zh: 不要让没有意义的事情占据你的时间、精力和热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, we are done.
zh: 好,我们结束了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, thank you all very much for coming.
zh: 好了,非常感谢大家前来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I leave you with just one thing, go build something you love.
zh: 如果我只留下一句话给你们,那就是:去构建你热爱的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go build something that should exist in the world.
zh: 去构建那些应该存在于这个世界上的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Leave this planet better than you found it.
zh: 让这个星球因你而变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you all very much.
zh: 非常感谢大家。
